name: Queen Victoria
hook: Britain's longest-reigning monarch before Elizabeth II, and the family, ministers and habits around her.

facts.label: 1837 to 1901
facts.statement: Victoria reigned from 1837 to 1901; when she died on January 22, 1901, Henry James wrote that everyone felt 'a bit motherless.'

facts.label: Prince Albert
facts.statement: Prince Albert was her German-born husband and consort; he popularized the Christmas tree and co-designed Osborne House.

facts.label: Edward VII
facts.statement: Her eldest son succeeded her in 1901 as Edward VII.

facts.label: Benjamin Disraeli
facts.statement: Benjamin Disraeli was her favorite prime minister — a novelist-turned-politician, twice PM, made Earl of Beaconsfield in 1876.

facts.label: chloroform
facts.statement: Victoria used chloroform in 1853 while giving birth to her eighth child, easing her royal birthing pains.

facts.label: Ottawa
facts.statement: She chose Ottawa as the capital of Canada on December 31, 1857.

facts.label: hemophilia
facts.statement: Victoria carried hemophilia; a granddaughter brought the blood disease into the Russian royal house.
